chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: Day jobs musicians held
summary: Few musicians had day jobs; those who did worked in stores or elevators, while many lived off gigs.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: MR. WELBURN: Who was some of the musicians who worked there, say, some of the day jobs that you can think of?
Or, what kinds of jobs? Possibly in the post office or factory?
In the post office, your -- I don't think very few of them worked as a mailman because that was too hard a strenuous job.
But most of them worked probably downtown. Maybe some of them worked in department stores or elevators, or something like that (inaudible).
Jobs that wouldn't interfere with their music, you know. Musicians back there proud (inaudible).
And then a lot of musicians that were gigging a lot, didn't work at all, because they were making enough money to take care of their family.
